subject: Application - Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Agent Engine (Dublin)
paragraphs: I am applying for the Senior Site Reliability Engineer role on the Agent Engine team in Dublin. The description reads like my own work with the nouns changed: a fleet that exists so that other people's workloads can run on it, where the failures that matter happen below the abstraction, and where the job is to make the platform boring for the teams on top of it. For the last three years my users have been other engineers, and what made my platform usable was not any single component but the rule that a change is only real once a gate has read the built artifact back.

That platform is one flake declaring thirteen NixOS hosts, with an SSH certificate authority, SOPS-encrypted secrets and a task interface as the operator surface. Reliability is recorded rather than assumed: a sentinel logs job status, generation age, disk and pressure-stall figures every fifteen minutes and pages on anything that is not ok, and the services on top are Go, Python and Bash. Most days I am reading systemd journals, nftables rules and TLS handshakes to find out why something that should be running is not, which is the part of this role I would enjoy most.

Three things I should be direct about. I do not operate a multi-tenant Kubernetes fleet today: my thirteen hosts are single-tenant and separated by role, and the isolation I have built is a certificate authority, per-host keys and a module boundary rather than namespaces, quotas and network policy. So the scheduler and the cluster API are where I would be learning rather than recognising, and debugging a pod that will not schedule is a different skill from debugging a unit that will not start. Cilium and Istio are equally unproven here: my networking is a WireGuard mesh, nftables and an internal CA, with no service mesh in production, and I would rather say that plainly than imply a depth I do not have.

I am based in south-west Germany, so Dublin means relocating, and I want to be as clear about that as about the technical gaps. I am a US citizen with German permanent residence, and that residence does not transfer to Ireland; the move needs an Irish employment permit and employer-supported relocation, which I would want to plan openly with your mobility team rather than discover at offer stage. Hybrid in Dublin is the model I am looking for. What draws me to Agent Engine is that tenant isolation for someone else's agents is a security problem before it is an operations one, and the platform I run has taught me how much of that comes down to keys, boundaries and the discipline of reading what actually happened. I would welcome the chance to talk through where that experience would and would not carry over.
